notes: The Call's 1910 Real Estate and Financial Section re-read a second time for the building-news, permit, contract and building-sale entries that give a corner or an offset but no lot dimension — the ones #407's re-read (sn85066387-1910-permits.json) explicitly left out because it took only the lot-bearing counterparts. Same 244-page span as #407 (the head page and the pages around it for every Saturday of 1910, from curiv_jenner, curiv_klamath, curiv_mecca and curiv_needles), scanned by a regex for corner/offset phrases with no adjacent lot-size pattern and then read by hand. Private owners, buyers, sellers and lessees are left out at extraction (cut from raw where the source names them); contractors, architects, institutions and named firms are kept. Corner and offset entries were placed with research/tools/corner.py --batch's new offset mode, added for this run: it matches the measured frontage start on the block face against the record's stated offset (within 4 ft) and the roll year (within 2 years, the tolerance already used elsewhere in the tool) when the record gives no lot to check against area. A bare corner with neither a lot nor an offset is not chosen between its parcels, per the tool's own docstring, and stays unresolved.

coverage.remaining: The weekly Building Contracts lists in 1911-1913 are metes-and-bounds and were read only for named buildings; they are the next corner.py batch (unchanged from the dossier's prior coverage note). Five Presidio Terrace tract-lot entries from the July-December 1910 batch are resolved separately, by a tract-lot-to-APN key documented in the dossier, not by this batch's offset method.
coverage.note: 311 candidate corner/offset windows surfaced by a regex scan of the 244 pages; after dropping leases (out of this batch's scope), loans that name no construction, Real Estate Transactions deeds at a nominal consideration, out-of-town locations, fires, duplicates of the run's own extraction, and passages that turned out to carry a lot dimension after all, 120 findings. 19 resolved (all by hand with corner.py --batch's offset mode), 4 of those declined as duplicates of entries this same source already published; 101 unresolved, nearly all bare corners with no lot or offset for the tool to choose between their parcels, or offset entries whose measured frontage and roll year match nothing on that block face.
